input.title: Widespread adoption of AI agents in knowledge work
input.description: What happens when AI agents can autonomously handle 80% of routine knowledge work tasks — email triage, report writing, scheduling, data analysis, code review — across most industries?

consequences.text: Workers redefine professional identity around judgment, creativity, and relationship-building rather than task execution, leading to widespread career existential crises.
Demand for AI infrastructure drives a new generation of specialized hardware, creating supply chain bottlenecks and geopolitical competition for chip manufacturing capacity.
Companies that adopt AI agents earliest capture disproportionate productivity gains, accelerating market concentration in every sector.
Energy consumption from always-on AI agents offsets efficiency gains from reduced commuting and office space, with net carbon impact depending on grid mix.
Governments struggle to adapt labor regulations, tax policy, and social safety nets to a workforce where humans and AI agents share responsibilities.
Liability frameworks collapse when AI agents make autonomous decisions — who is responsible when an agent sends the wrong email, approves a bad contract, or leaks sensitive data?
Power asymmetry grows between those who control AI agents and those who don't, raising fundamental questions about consent, autonomy, and digital self-determination.
New forms of mentorship emerge where senior professionals teach AI-collaboration skills rather than task-specific knowledge, fundamentally changing how expertise is transmitted.
Mid-tier consulting, accounting, and legal firms face existential pressure as AI agents deliver comparable output at a fraction of the cost, forcing consolidation or specialization.
A new gig economy emerges around AI agent configuration, training, and oversight — 'agent wranglers' become a major employment category.
Countries that heavily regulate AI agents lose competitive advantage to those that don't, creating a regulatory race to the bottom internationally.
Insurance industry develops new 'AI liability' products, creating a multi-billion dollar market but also normalizing the risks of autonomous AI decision-making.
Open-source AI agent frameworks democratize access, enabling small teams to compete with enterprises — but also lower the barrier for malicious use.
Universal basic income debates shift from theoretical to urgent as traditional employment models break down faster than new ones emerge.
Society develops new norms around 'AI transparency' — disclosing when work was done by an agent becomes as expected as disclosing conflicts of interest.

consequences.title: Agent audit trails
consequences.text: Create open-source 'AI agent audit trails' that log every decision an agent makes, enabling accountability without sacrificing speed. Could be mandated by regulators.

consequences.title: HITL certification
consequences.text: Develop a 'human-in-the-loop' certification standard for AI agent deployments, where organizations commit to meaningful human oversight at critical decision points.
